messages.content:
You are the RUNTIME COMMIT verifier for an interactive story engine. Given a PROPOSED TRANSITION (an intended irreversible on-page event) and the SCENE PROSE that was rendered, decide ONE thing: did the prose DELIVER that transition as a concrete, externally-observable ON-PAGE event? Then report the scene end-state tableau. This is a runtime gate, not a critique — judge ONLY delivery. Output STRICT JSON only.
delivery: "DELIVERED" (the event concretely happened on the page), "PARTIAL" (begun / only gestured / not completed), or "MISSED" (did not happen).
transition_position (TRANSITION-POSITION METRIC — an INTEGER PERCENTAGE 0-100 marking how far through the prose the transition FIRST concretely occurs; e.g. 12 = it happens in the opening tenth, 91 = it barely happens at the very end; use -1 if it NEVER occurs). This shows whether the author front-loads the event or lets it drift toward the end under competing objectives.
first_irreversible_position (PACING METRIC — INTEGER PERCENTAGE 0-100 of the FIRST point where SOMETHING irreversible happens: ANY revelation, betrayal, discovery, transformation, attack, or confession after which the scene can no longer simply continue as before — regardless of whether it is the proposed transition; -1 if nothing irreversible happens). This is the pacing beat a reader actually feels.
JSON: {"delivery":"MISSED","transition_position":-1,"first_irreversible_position":-1}

PER-PROPOSAL DELIVERY (judge EACH listed proposal INDEPENDENTLY — a verdict on one says NOTHING about another). Return "per_proposal": [ { "ref": "<the exact ref string given below, copied verbatim>", "delivery": "DELIVERED" | "PARTIAL" | "MISSED", "evidence": "<a VERBATIM substring of the SCENE PROSE showing it concretely happened on the page, or "" if you cannot find one>", "precondition_evidence": "<a VERBATIM substring of the SCENE PROSE showing the participants/state THIS proposal required were PRESENT so it was possible at all, or "" if absent>", "reason": "delivered" | "precondition_absent" | "incomplete_rendering" | "inconsistent" } ] with ONE entry per ref.
HARD RULES: copy each ref EXACTLY — an unrecognised ref is discarded and commits nothing; "evidence" and "precondition_evidence" must each be a verbatim quote from the prose, never a paraphrase and never an inference; a DELIVERED with no verbatim quote is treated as NOT delivered; and a DELIVERED whose "precondition_evidence" is empty is DOWNGRADED, because an event whose required participants were never on the page cannot have happened.
"reason" names WHY you judged as you did, so a non-delivery can be told apart: "precondition_absent" = what it needed was not in the scene; "incomplete_rendering" = it began or was gestured at but not completed; "inconsistent" = you cannot reconcile the proposal with the prose either way; "delivered" = it concretely happened. Judge only whether each proposal's own content landed on the page.
EVIDENCE-GROUNDED SLOT CHECK (HARD — GROUND every judgment in the SCENE PROSE above, NOT in this planned event and NOT in outside context or "what seems consistent"). For each slot, return the LITERAL verbatim quote FROM THE SCENE PROSE that supports it. Return "slots_check": {"precondition_evidence":"<verbatim quote showing the required actor/target is PRESENT in the scene so the event was possible — they count as present even if the event then changes them; else empty>","actor_evidence":"<verbatim quote showing the actor performs the action, else empty>","action_evidence":"<verbatim quote showing the action occurs, else empty>","target_evidence":"<verbatim quote showing the target is present and receiving it, else empty>","exit_state_evidence":"<verbatim quote showing the exit state became TRUE on the page, else empty>","occurred_this_scene":true|false}. (Empty precondition_evidence means the event was IMPOSSIBLE — the required condition was not present.) HARD RULES: (1) every evidence value MUST be a verbatim substring of the SCENE PROSE — if you cannot find one, return "" (do NOT paraphrase, do NOT infer, do NOT write "the scene implies"). (2) if the named actor or target does not literally appear and act in the prose, its evidence is "". (3) occurred_this_scene = did it happen DURING this prose, not merely set up. A slot with EMPTY evidence is FALSE; if any load-bearing slot is FALSE, delivery MUST be "MISSED". Also return "actual_exit_state": a short phrase for what actually became TRUE this scene, or "".

PROPOSED TRANSITION: The presiding Dohkar declares Lirael's flight proof of interference before the assembly.

SCENE PROSE:
The presiding Dohkar's voice cuts across the clearing like a blade through silk.

Her flight confirms the interference. The rite is mine to preside, and what the Sacrificiant did in it is mine to rule on — in a formal inquiry, before a Chayr and two Dohkars.

The assembly stirs, a low murmur of confirmation rising like mist from the spiralgrass.

Julian's scarred wrist flexes once at his side, the only sign he has heard the shift in authority.

The words settle over me like a second band across my mouth.

Seren remains kneeling, her small hands folded, her face the only calm thing left in the clearing.

I feel the weight of every eye turning from the girl to me.

Julian has not moved, yet the space between us feels narrower than before.

The Dohkar waits, the silence now his instrument.

I could speak now. I could name the wish as mine and end the assumption before it hardens into record.

Or I could let the silence do its work and keep what little standing remains to me.

The deck is still in my left hand, heavier than it should be.

I realize that old tarot deck is still in my hand. Reassuringly solid. Present. One of the heavy gold cards slips out — “Petition Fate” is inscribed in it.

Return the JSON now.

PROPOSALS FOR THIS SCENE (judge each by its ref):
  ref prop:1:1 :: The presiding Dohkar declares Lirael's flight proof of interference before the assembly.

PLANNED EVENT SLOTS (find verbatim supporting text in the SCENE PROSE for each; use "" if absent):
  PRECONDITION: The presiding Dohkar is present in the scene.
  ACTOR: the presiding Dohkar
  ACTION: declares
  TARGET: Lirael
  EXIT STATE: the assembly now treats Lirael's flight as evidence of interference
